texts.facts: It is submitted by counsel for applicants that applicant no.1 Suchit Chourasiya has already expired on 27.04.2023, therefore, prays for deletion of his name. The counsel for applicants has also filed a copy of death certificate of applicant no.1 along with M.Cr.C.No.45072/2018. The death of applicant no.1 has also not been disputed by respondent no.2. Accordingly, the verbal prayer made by the counsel for applicants for deletion of name of applicant no.l is hereby allowed. The necessary amendment be made in the Court itself. Accordingly, application filed on behalf of applicant No.1 Sushit Chourasiya is hereby dismissed as abated. Heard on merits. This application under section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking following relief(s):- "(i) To allow this application. (ii) To quash the FIR registered in Crime No 337/2017 for offences punishable under Section 498-A, 506, and 34 of IPC and section 3/4 of dowry prohibition Act. (iii) To quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the Criminal proceedings pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class Chhindwara in RCT No. 906/17 parties being Criminal case o "State of M.P. vs Suchit Chourasiya & others" in the interest of justice." 2. By this application, the applicants have challenged the FIR in Crime No. 337/2017 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Chhindwara for offence under Sections 498-A, 506, 34 of IPC and Suchit Chourasiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115249145/ 2 under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act as well as RCT No. 906/2017 pending in the Court of JMFC, Chhindwara. 3. According to the prosecution case, the respondent No.2 was married to applicant No.1, who has expired during the pendency of this application on 28.5.2013. It is alleged that on the instigations of the applicants No. 2, 3 and 4, applicant No.1 started demanding Dowry and also used to beat her. He also started excessively consuming liquor and he was in the habit of consuming sleeping pills or her jewelry was mortgaged. In the meanwhile, the respondent No.2 gave birth to a boy on 22.03.2014. The entire delivery expenses were borne by her parents as she was forcibly left in her parental house by the applicant No.1 at the instigation of the applicants No. 2 to 4. Thereafter an agreement for settlement was executed on 03.09.2015 and again she shifted to her matrimonial house. However, on 03.04.2017, she was badly beaten by the applicants No.1 and 2 and was ousted from her matrimonial house. Somehow, she managed to come back to her parental home. On 28.05.2017, the applicant No.1 came to her parental home and insisted that she should come along with an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- otherwise she should not come to her matrimonial house. When, respondent No.2 expressed the inability of her parents to fulfill his demand, then she was badly beaten by applicant No.1 in the parental home of respondent No.2 and he insisted that unless and until she brings an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-, she will not be allowed to stay in her matrimonial house. She is residing in her parental home and is waiting of her in-laws to come and to take her back but they did not turn back. Accordingly, FIR has been lodged. 4. It is submitted by counsel for applicants that the allegations made in the complaint are false. In fact, a compromise was arrived between the respondent No.2 and applicant No.1 and from thereafter respondent No.2 was residing peacefully in her matrimonial house.
texts.arguments: Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for respondents. It is submitted that there are specific allegations against the applicants. The trial is already going on and, therefore, the proceedings may not be [LEAKAGE_MASK].
